subsystems.name: Alternative genetic polymers
subsystems.role: store and pass on information in molecular backbones other than DNA or RNA.
parts: sugar- and backbone-modified nucleic acids (e.g. TNA, GNA, HNA, PNA, FANA)
reverse transcription back into DNA for sequencing

subsystems.name: Expanded genetic alphabets
subsystems.role: add extra 'letters' beyond A, T, G and C.
parts: hydrophobic base pairs that stack without hydrogen bonding
nucleotide importers and triphosphate transporters for cells

subsystems.name: Chassis and containment
subsystems.role: a host cell that carries the new chemistry without escaping or dying.
parts: dependency on an unnatural building block

subsystems.name: Orthogonal translation
subsystems.role: read the extra letters into protein, not just store them.

subsystems.name: Selection and evolution
subsystems.role: find which unnatural molecules actually do something useful.
parts: in-vitro selection from large random libraries

buildSteps.title: Design the chemistry
buildSteps.detail: Choose a base pair or backbone whose pairing is specific, and check that natural enzymes will not confuse it with DNA.

buildSteps.title: Make the monomers
buildSteps.detail: Synthesise the unnatural nucleoside triphosphates and, if the design calls for it, unnatural amino acids, in quantities and purity good enough for enzymes to use.

buildSteps.title: Evolve a polymerase
buildSteps.detail: Take a natural polymerase and mutate and select it until it can copy the unnatural polymer and reverse-transcribe it back — the essential tool for reading and writing the new information.

buildSteps.title: Work in a test tube first
buildSteps.detail: Run replication, selection and amplification cycles in vitro to see whether the new polymer can fold, bind targets or catalyse reactions.

buildSteps.title: Put it inside a cell
buildSteps.detail: Introduce the extra base pair and its transporter into a chassis organism, and select for cells that keep the unnatural letter through division.

buildSteps.title: Wire it into translation
buildSteps.detail: Engineer tRNAs and ribosomes so the extra letters are read as codons, giving proteins containing chemistry that natural life cannot make.

buildSteps.title: Build in containment
buildSteps.detail: Make survival depend on an unnatural nutrient, so the organism cannot persist if it leaves the bioreactor.

buildSteps.title: Iterate toward useful output
buildSteps.detail: Once the system is stable and contained, tune it to produce a specific molecule, enzyme or material.

prerequisites.tech: Chemical DNA synthesis and cheap sequencing
prerequisites.why: every designed gene, library and readout depends on them.
no natural enzyme copies unnatural backbones well enough; they must be bred in the lab.
chemically synthesised and reduced genomes have been made, but they are still fragile and slow to build.
a handful of non-standard amino acids can be inserted today; a full parallel genetic code cannot.

prerequisites.tech: Predictive models of unnatural biopolymer folding
prerequisites.why: without them, designs for new enzymes and structures are mostly trial and error.

pathway.milestone: unnatural nucleic acids that evolve and bind targets in a test tube, and bacterial cells that carry one extra base pair
pathway.unlocks: proof that information can be stored and copied outside the standard four-letter system.

pathway.milestone: semi-synthetic organisms that genuinely need the extra letters to live
pathway.unlocks: biocontainment — organisms that cannot survive in the wild.

pathway.milestone: organisms whose expanded code is read into proteins at useful yields
pathway.unlocks: enzymes and materials with properties natural biology does not offer.

pathway.milestone: stable alternative-biochemistry platforms for manufacturing, including mirror-image molecules
pathway.unlocks: new drugs, catalysts and materials, produced under strict containment.
